stories.body: Houthi forces have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government, according to military and government sources. Saudi-backed forces announced their withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb area to reinforce the city, leaving the Houthis in control of strategically important territory at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. The retreat follows weeks of fighting over a shipping route that has become increasingly important for Saudi oil exports amid the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The UN estimates that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen.
stories.headline: Houthis advance towards Aden as government forces abandon key Red Sea positions

stories.body: Estonia will close all three of its border crossings with Russia from December 1 after authorities accused Russia’s GRU military intelligence service of ordering an attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Eight people were detained on Saturday during an alleged attempt to cause an explosion and fire; the company’s security team intervened, and authorities reported no injuries or damage. Prime Minister Kristen Michal linked the incident to Estonia’s support for Ukraine. The closure has no announced end date and follows an August arson attack on another defence company that Estonian authorities also attributed to Russian intelligence.
stories.headline: Estonia to close Russian border after alleged sabotage attempt at drone factory

stories.body: Hundreds of thousands of people gathered in Prague on Sunday against plans to replace public broadcasting licence fees with funding from the state budget. Organisers put attendance at roughly 350,000 to 400,000. Critics argue that the proposal would expose Czech Television and Czech Radio to political pressure, while the proposed funding would also represent a cut of about 15%. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš denies seeking editorial control and says the funding system needs updating. The rally follows weeks of demonstrations and a strike by broadcasting staff after the bill passed its first parliamentary reading in late October.
stories.headline: Hundreds of thousands rally in Prague against public media funding overhaul

stories.body: Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel’s next government, demanded Benjamin Netanyahu’s immediate departure following allegations that the caretaker prime minister’s office helped trigger unfounded arrests before the October 27 election. Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu’s chief of staff directed police to a source whose claims led to warrantless raids and the arrest of three members of the Arab-led Ra’am party; they were subsequently released after police found the information unfounded. Eisenkot called for an investigation, while Likud accused him of incitement. The dispute erupted hours after representatives held unity-government talks, with neither bloc yet securing a parliamentary majority.
stories.headline: Eisenkot demands Netanyahu’s departure after report of election interference

stories.body: Singapore-based Megaspeed says Alice Huang left her executive role on August 30, 2025, and has no current position at the company, disputing reports about its operations and commissioning an external legal investigation. The major Nvidia customer faces scrutiny over possible breaches of US chip export restrictions following Jensen Huang’s resignation amid reported affairs and allegations that Alice Huang acted for Chinese intelligence. Beijing denies the espionage allegations, and Alice Huang has not publicly commented. Singapore says its investigation into Megaspeed continues. Separately, a US congressional committee chairman said Jensen Huang has agreed to testify privately before three House committees.
stories.headline: Megaspeed disputes allegations as scrutiny of Nvidia ties intensifies

stories.body: More than 2,400 US flights were cancelled and 8,800 delayed on Sunday as airlines continued recovering from Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said normal operations might not return until Monday because aircraft and crews remained out of position. He said a router installed during a communications upgrade in El Dorado, Arkansas, flooded the network with faulty signals, although investigators were still determining the root cause and responsibility. Friday’s suspension lasted about four and a half hours and disrupted international connections. President Donald Trump urged Congress to provide additional funding to modernise air traffic control.
stories.headline: US flight disruptions continue as airlines recover from nationwide ground stop

stories.body: A Politico poll conducted by PF Global after the midterms found sharply different reactions to Republican losses among Trump’s 2024 voters. Those identifying with MAGA generally favoured moving closer to the president, while non-MAGA Trump voters preferred a different direction; about one in five in the latter group said they voted for Democrats this time. A majority of non-MAGA Trump voters blamed his actions in office for the defeats. The findings highlight the difficulty Republicans face in retaining Trump’s loyal base while recovering less committed voters ahead of 2028.
stories.headline: Post-midterm poll exposes divisions within Trump’s electoral coalition

stories.body: The Washington Post reports that rising measles cases are confronting doctors with conditions they have not previously treated, with some of the greatest uncertainties involving the youngest patients. The supplied excerpt does not identify specific complications or provide case numbers.
stories.headline: Measles surge presents unfamiliar cases and uncertainty for doctors

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez presented an election programme pledging to devote 1% of GDP to social housing and introduce a national child-rearing benefit, adopting proposals previously championed by coalition partner Sumar. At a rally in Alcorcón ahead of the November 29 election, he also proposed higher taxes on investment funds and large landlords holding empty homes, operating tourist apartments or charging unaffordable rents. A separate care benefit would cover four weeks at 100% of the statutory earnings base for parents of children under eight. Other commitments include legal recognition of mutual care arrangements between friends and constitutional protection for inflation-linked pensions and abortion rights.
stories.headline: PSOE pledges social housing investment and new support for parents

stories.body: Alberto Núñez Feijóo will visit Gipuzkoa on Tuesday to support PP congressional candidate Jon Echeverría after a group threw firecrackers, eggs and stones during a campaign visit to Hernani, forcing the event’s cancellation. Police escorted the candidate away. Basque premier Imanol Pradales and PNV leader Aitor Esteban condemned the attack, and the PSOE issued a condemnation on Sunday. Feijóo criticised the Basque Socialists and EH Bildu and accused Sánchez of relying on partners linked to intimidation, without the reports establishing their involvement in the attack. The PP hopes to regain a Gipuzkoa seat for the first time since 2011.
stories.headline: Feijóo changes campaign schedule after attack on PP candidate in Hernani

stories.body: Vox leader Santiago Abascal told a rally in Cornellà de Llobregat that his party would accept the November 29 election result if there were no cheating, while accusing Pedro Sánchez of preparing fraud and violence. The report presents no evidence supporting those allegations. Abascal also attacked the government’s economic and immigration policies and appealed to voters across party lines, including Catalan nationalists, as Aliança Catalana is not contesting the election. The venue reached capacity, while around 50 antifascist demonstrators protested outside.
stories.headline: Abascal makes acceptance of election result conditional on absence of fraud

stories.body: Barcelona’s Guardia Urbana, supported by the Mossos d’Esquadra, peacefully cleared the housing protest encampment in Plaça de Catalunya shortly after midnight on Monday. Around 80 people were identified, with no complaints or citations reported, and social services attended alongside cleaning crews. The city cited safety, sanitation and access concerns after 47 days of occupation, while organisers denounced the eviction as unlawful and carried out without warning or mediation. The camp had increasingly sheltered homeless and vulnerable people. Mayor Jaume Collboni had also recently called for the square to be available for normal Christmas celebrations.
stories.headline: Police clear Plaça de Catalunya housing encampment after 47 days

stories.body: Traffic authority figures obtained by El Periódico show that accumulated congestion on the Ronda de Dalt rose 79.1% between 2019 and 2025, while vehicle numbers increased just 4.7%. Congestion on the Ronda Litoral rose 54.1%. The figures add together delays across different road sections, rather than measuring continuous hours of traffic jams. Trànsit says demand exceeds capacity, leaving both roads vulnerable to disruption from minor incidents. The busiest recurring periods remain 7–9 a.m., 1–3 p.m. and 5–7 p.m.; average speeds have fallen on both routes.
stories.headline: Congestion on Barcelona’s Ronda de Dalt rises 79% despite modest traffic growth

stories.body: Works on the Meridiana bridges will close a 300-metre stretch of Via Favència overnight through November 22. Closures run from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with Sunday restrictions beginning at midnight. The project includes improvements to the pedestrian bridge and its approaches as part of Nou Barris maintenance works. The signed diversion takes drivers via the Meridiana service road, a turnaround at Avinguda de Rio de Janeiro, Passeig de Santa Coloma and Passeig de Torras i Bages before rejoining the Ronda de Dalt at entrance 1.
stories.headline: Overnight Via Favència closures continue through November 22

stories.body: More frequent floods, torrential rain and fires are straining local government finances, according to municipal leaders and finance specialists interviewed by El Periódico. Rubí mayor and Arc Metropolità president Ana María Martínez called for larger contingency budgets and additional funding, warning that emergency spending can displace other services. Experts said delayed aid often forces councils to advance recovery costs or borrow. Proposed responses include a regional emergency fund providing rapid liquidity, more spending on prevention and changes to fiscal rules governing exceptional disaster costs. The report announces no specific tax increase.
stories.headline: Extreme weather puts mounting pressure on municipal budgets
